title: bug: the foundation attempt-windows launch arm has ~60s of margin over real provider latency
description:
Commissioned by governor-12ae245c on owner instruction (2026-09-08), replacing ARCHIVED task-0bd37766500c427aacf4f59abbd6dad1. That row named the wrong mechanism; this one carries the finding that survived it. Read this whole description before planning — two architect seats already burned on the archived row's premise.

WHAT THE ARCHIVED ROW GOT WRONG. It claimed `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861` reds the daemon leg once `apps/daemon/src` reaches 592 test files, and asked for a repro at that count. Both halves are falsified:
- architect-f362f7a6 ran the UNCHANGED 592-file suite to EXIT 0 — 592 passed, 10572 tests, 370.34s.
- `find apps/daemon/src -name "*.test.ts" | wc -l` is 596 today. The 592 count cannot be reached again without deleting four peer-owned files, which no seat may do. Those four additions are themselves count/count+1 evidence with no recurrence.
Do not re-open the file-count theory. It was measured and it is dead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY FRAGILE (architect-5385678f, comment-eaa1af5ee7c34d43b92d9ce92019bdd7). The case at :861 launches a REAL provider session child, so the child's latency is the provider's. The arm's own comment at :836-842 records observed launches of 100s and 122s on this host, and says the old 120_000 bound was "a coin flip" and that 240_000 "keeps a real bound". That leaves roughly 60 SECONDS of margin against a latency the repo does not control. That margin — not test-file count — is what makes this arm red intermittently under load.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, both load-bearing for whoever plans this:
1. The effective bound is NOT the package script's `--testTimeout=30000`. This case overrides it with an explicit per-case `}, 300_000);` at :942, and the launch timeout inside it is 240_000. Any analysis starting from 30000 is starting from the wrong number.
2. The arm is reachable ONLY on a win32 host with an installed provable Claude runtime. At :816-819 it returns early asserting CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING otherwise. On a runtime-less host this case is a no-op, so a green leg there proves nothing about it.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` is the owned-package gate for every row touching apps/daemon. When this arm flares, it names a file the failing row never touched, and that row pays multi-run cycles attributing a red that is not its own. It has not recurred over the last four added files, which is why this is filed MEDIUM rather than HIGH — it is latent, not live. Promote it when a seat is free; do not let a future red get misattributed for a third time.

ORIGINAL SYMPTOM REPORT, preserved for whoever needs the shape of the failure: filed by worker-319873d7 out of task-bd2f1ecf. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` exited 1 with exactly one failure, `foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861:24 expect(outcome.ok).toBe(true)` received false, reproduced back to back at 733.80s and 414.69s. The failing file ALONE with `--testTimeout=30000` passed explicitly: EXIT 0, 8 tests, 171.40s. Excluding a DIFFERENT file cleared the red just as well as excluding the newly added one — which is what pointed at co-scheduling rather than any file's content, and is also why the file-count reading looked plausible at the time.
definitionOfDone: Measure the launch duration at :861 fresh, foreground, on the verifying host, and quote the numbers. The arm's 100s/122s comment is a record, not a measurement you may inherit - confirm or correct it. Do NOT attempt a file-count repro: the unchanged suite ran EXIT 0 at 592 files (592 passed, 10572 tests, 370.34s) and there are 596 files today.

State whether the arm actually EXECUTED on the verifying host. At :816-819 it returns early asserting CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING when no provable Claude runtime is installed, so on a runtime-less host this case is a no-op and a green leg is vacuous evidence for it. Record which case applies, with the evidence that distinguishes them.

Remove the arm's dependence on unbounded provider latency WITHOUT weakening what it asserts. It must still assert that settlement released the worktree, that the boundary was actually reached, and that the launch was a real provider session on whichever lane still runs it. Deleting the arm, skipping it, marking it conditional on a green-only host, or reducing it to 'did not throw' is not a fix - see global rail 1.

Justify the bound you land, in seconds, against the latency you measured, and state the remaining margin. The real bound today is the 240_000 launch timeout inside the explicit per-case `}, 300_000);` at :942 - the package script's --testTimeout=30000 does NOT apply to this case, so do not reason from it. A larger number chosen without a measurement behind it just re-arms the next row; say why that number and not another.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 foreground with the `Test Files N passed` count line quoted, at the CURRENT file count AND at count+1 (add one throwaway trivial test file, prove EXIT 0, then remove it). Disclose any foreign red with path attribution rather than calling the leg green.
reopenReason: Governor promote BACKLOG -> PLANNING to keep the claim pool stocked. This is the correctly-framed successor to ARCHIVED task-0bd37766, whose file-count premise was falsified. Read the description before planning: the 592-file theory is written down AS DEAD (unchanged suite ran EXIT 0 at 592 files, 596 files on disk today) and the real subject is the ~60s margin between the 240_000 launch bound at foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861 and observed 100-122s provider latency. Two architect seats already burned on the dead premise; do not re-open it, and do not widen the bound without a measurement behind the number.
